title: Chapter 43 — Hark!
paragraphs: "PSST! Did you hear that noise, Cabaco?"

It was the middle watch, in fair moonlight. The seamen were standing in a line stretching from one of the freshwater casks in the waist to the scuttlebutt (the drinking-water cask) near the taffrail. In this way they passed the buckets along to fill the scuttlebutt. Standing, for the most part, on the sacred ground of the quarter-deck, they were careful not to speak or shuffle their feet. From hand to hand the buckets went in the deepest silence, broken only by the occasional flap of a sail and the steady hum of the ceaselessly advancing keel.
It was in the middle of this calm that Archy, one of the line, whose station was near the after-hatches, whispered the words above to the man next to him, a Cholo.
"Psst! Did you hear that noise, Cabaco?"
"Take the bucket, will you, Archy? What noise do you mean?"
"There it is again — under the hatches — don't you hear it — a cough — it sounded like a cough."
"Cough be damned! Pass along that return bucket."
"There again — there it is! — it sounds like two or three sleepers turning over!"
"Caramba! Knock it off, shipmate, will you? It's the three soaked biscuits you ate for supper turning over inside you — nothing else. Watch the bucket!"
"Say what you want, shipmate. I've got sharp ears."
"Right, you're the one, aren't you, who heard the hum of the old Quaker lady's knitting needles fifty miles at sea from Nantucket. You're the one."

"Grin away. We'll see what turns up. Listen, Cabaco — there is somebody down in the after-hold who has not yet been seen on deck. And I suspect our old Mogul knows something about it too. I heard Stubb tell Flask, one morning watch, that there was something of that sort in the wind."
